newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
Indonesia has secured the return of five paintings allegedly stolen from the National Museum in Jakarta. The paintings were to be auctioned by Christie's in Singapore early next month.

Australia has appointed John McCarthy, currently ambassador to the United States, as the new head of its Indonesian mission. The posting of McCarthy comes after the previous candidate for the post, Miles Kupa, was turned down by Jakarta on the grounds that he was critical of President Suharto.

Every government employee must persuade another ten people to vote for the ruling Golkar party in next year's general elections, chairman of the organisation of government workers (KORPRI), Suryatna Subrata, said. Government workers are expected to vote for Golkar, one of three parties legally entitled to contest elections.
It is rumoured that President Suharto's daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana may be set to buy timber tycoon Prayogo Pangestu's stake in the car manufacturer Astra.
State-owned Bank BNI is expected to allocate around 500 million shares, or some 50 percent of total shares to be floated on the local exchanges in November, for pension funds and insurance firms.
